title: Age-Related Macular Degeneration (AMD): The Comprehensive Clinical Guide
summary: AMD is the leading cause of irreversible blindness in developed nations, characterized by progressive degeneration of the retinal pigment epithelium and photoreceptors. This guide covers the spectrum from dry drusen formation to neovascular exudative disease.

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup Sequence
content: Step 1: BCVA and Amsler Grid testing
Step 3: OCT Macular Cube (to detect subretinal/intraretinal fluid)
Step 4: Fundus Autofluorescence (FAF) for GA mapping
Step 5: Fluorescein Angiography (FFA) / OCT-Angiography to localize CNV

sections.title: Management Principles
content: AREDS2 Formulation: Vit C 500mg, Vit E 400IU, Zinc 80mg, Copper 2mg, Lutein 10mg, Zeaxanthin 2mg.
Anti-VEGF intravitreal injections (Ranibizumab, Aflibercept, Brolucizumab, Faricimab).
Treat-and-Extend (T&E) dosing protocol to minimize injection burden.
Lifestyle: Smoking cessation is the single most critical modification.

content.explanation: D: Deposits (sub-RPE), R: Retinal pigment epithelium changes, U: Unilateral or bilateral, S: Scotoma (central), E: Exudative risk, N: Neovascularization.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Smoking increases risk of progression to advanced AMD by 2-3x.
Always check the fellow eye: the risk of developing CNV in a fellow eye of a patient with unilateral neovascular AMD is ~10% per year.
Brolucizumab (Beovu) carries a higher risk of intraocular inflammation and retinal vasculitis—monitor closely.
Geographic Atrophy (GA) is currently managed with C3/C5 inhibitors (e.g., Pegcetacoplan) following recent FDA approvals.
